item.title: GTA 6 launch week revenue predicted to top the biggest movies from Star Wars, Harry Potter, and LOTR
item.summary: And it seems like a pretty good bet after becoming the most pre-ordered game on Sony and Microsoft's digital stores
item.text:
At long last, GTA 6 is finally here, and wouldn't you believe it – not only is it rather good, but it's also pretty popular. That wasn't unexpected, of course, and if one market intelligence and analyst firm's launch-week prediction proves accurate, Rockstar could be on track to earn more than the biggest Star Wars, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter movies combined.
This is an observation highlighted by Gearbox boss Randy Pitchford, who writes on Twitter: "Newzoo's forecast is that GTA VI will generate more in its launch week than the entire original theatrical runs of the most successful Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, Star Wars movies combined."
He appears to be citing Newzoo's July estimate, following the game's pre-orders going live. At the time, it was predicted that GTA 6 could earn between $3.3 billion and $5.2 billion in total sales by the end of its launch week.
Rockstar hasn't released any official data yet, but it's clear that GTA 6 is off to an exceptional start. Before launch, Sony and Microsoft confirmed that it was the most pre-ordered game of all time on their respective digital stores, and market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates that, as of yesterday, it had sold 17.07 million units and brought in $1.65 billion in revenue.
So, how does that compare to the movies Pitchford highlights? Per Box Office Mojo, the single most successful movies (by lifetime box office revenue) from each franchise are Star Wars: The Force Awakens, The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King, and Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 2. The worldwide lifetime gross revenue for each of those comes in at around $2.07 billion, $1.12 billion, and $1.34 billion, respectively, for a combined total of about $4.53 billion.
If Sensor Tower's most recent estimate is correct, then GTA 6 hasn't reached this high just yet, but we're only just on launch day – Newzoo was allowing for the full week in its previous forecast. And, if the analytics firm ends up being correct, then it could be on track to earn over half a billion dollars more than those movies in its first days, which is wild.
With 10/10 GTA 6 reviews almost across the board, though, it's a deserved result for Rockstar. We'll just have to wait and see how high that number can go.

item.title: GameStop CEO slams 'code-in-a-box' games in the wake of GTA 6's discless release
item.summary: Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses. Read more
item.text:
Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.
In an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop."
These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.
Cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their plans. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition."
Though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.
Of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony plans to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.
Disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.
If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

The downloadable version is now officially available for free on the GTA 6 website, and there's even a special "printable" option for those who don't just want to look at it in digital form.
It comes with a big version of the GTA 6 cover art as well - you can see both of these down below:
The physical edition still isn't available yet, but Rockstar Games says that it will be "made available at the Rockstar Store shortly after launch". We'll keep an eye out and update this article when that happens.
Honestly, I don't think the map is that great, as I hoped it might include some places of interest rather than just each region that's available to visit, but as a poster on a wall, it's still worth displaying somewhere.
I'd rather wait for the physical version, but it's certainly nice that it exists as a freebie as well.

item.title: Looking for free guns and body armor in GTA 6? Try the trunks of cop cars
item.summary: Loot your local cruiser for longarms and even body armor.
item.text:
Remember how stealing a cop car in the older GTA games used to get you a free shotgun? Well, turns out Vice City's police force is even better armed. If you need some extra guns quickly, particularly shotguns and assault rifles, filching them from the trunk of a police car is a great method, though obviously it comes with certain risks.
You might have realised, but stealing cars in GTA 6 is significantly more complicated than previous games, especially if they're alarmed. Thankfully, this doesn't apply to any police pickup trucks like the Bravado Bison the cops sometimes use, which you'll spot occasionally both in rural areas and in the city
With the police pickups, you can simply climb onto the bed at the back and open the storage crate, grabbing any weapons and ammo inside, including other potential items like Stun Guns, without setting off any alarms.
For proper police cruisers, though, their trunks are alarmed along with the doors, meaning you'll need a tool to deal with them, the slim jim, which you get during the "Moses" mission in Chapter 2. If you slim jim the door of the cop car and get inside, the trunk will unlock, so you can head around the back, interact to open it, and steal whatever's in the boot without tackling the alarm, whether it be an assault rifle, shotgun, or even body armor.
If you don't have the slim jim yet, you can still open the trunk (you'll see your character use a screwdriver) but the alarm will go off.
Once you've collected the weapons, you can interact with your own car trunk, and you'll see a prompt to stow the weapons inside. You'll be rather conspicuous wandering around with an assault rifle in your hands or strapped to your back, after all.
Obviously, it's best not to try and steal cop cars with cops in them, but you can find them around, or parked at police stations, such as in Port Gellhorn or Vice City.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
More generally, it's definitely worth looting random car trunks to see what you can find. Sometimes they contain cash, drugs, handguns, or consumables—just make sure to scan them with the Wainkit App first (which you're introduced to in Chapter 1) to tell if they're alarmed or not, and whether you can break in without the slim jim.

item.title: GTA 6's shockingly accurate Instagram memes make fun of Rockstar's delays and more
item.summary: It's basically the first "we got x before GTA 7" meme
item.text:
GTA 6's fake Instagram shitposts, which include Rockstar Games clowning on how long the game took to release, are proving to be a highlight of the whole experience for many.
GTA games are generally developed as a time capsule of what culture was like at the time, so while GTA 5 definitely had some social media influence in it, things have certainly changed in the time since that game was released 13 years ago.
GTA 6 on the other hand goes all in, with takes on WhatsApp, Instagram, and a Shazam for cars called WAInk. On top of that, when you go to bed in-game, Jason doesn't go to sleep – he instead starts looking at the phone and scrolling aimlessly.
But since 2013, social media shitposting has become the norm, and GTA 6's version of Instagram is shockingly accurate. Real social media has been filled with screenshots of the posts found on Snapmatic, with Rockstar's famous attention to detail shining through.
Highlights of my own playthrough have been an image of a Batman-esque hero holding down a villain with the caption "me when I find the guy who shit my pants," a woman looking seductive with the caption "how the emergency door latch looks at me on the plane," while real social media highlights abstract memes and a certified @mr.queef classic: a speedometer maxed out with "me when I get a call that my wife is giving birth (I'm omw to the casino)."
However, Rockstar has also poked fun at itself through this meme onslaught, with its own take on the "we got x before GTA 6 meme." One post shows a Paw Patrol-like game titled Barnyard Blue Hot Fursuit with the caption, "Barnyard Blue video game before Race and Chase 7 is crazy." Another shows the different types of headaches, with a full head one captioned with "Race and Chase 7 delayed another year."
Funnily enough, Race'n'Chase was the original name for the game in development that would eventually become Grand Theft Auto. So basically, Rockstar made the first "we got x before GTA 7" joke.
